newsitem.title: USA: Fair weather forecast for U.S. shuttle.
newsitem.headline: Fair weather forecast for U.S. shuttle.

text.p: Launch pad workers resumed the countdown for Tuesday's planned blastoff of space shuttle Columbia, NASA officials said on Monday.
The countdown clocks at Florida's Kennedy Space Centre began ticking down at 1 a.m. EST (0600 GMT) on Monday, said NASA spokesman George Diller.

U.S. Air Force meteorologists were predicting dry conditions and little wind for Columbia's planned 2:53 p.m. EST (1953 GMT) blastoff on Tuesday. They forecast an 80 percent chance of acceptable weather for launch.
The shuttle's countdown had been on hold since last Wednesday because of stormy weather, which brought high winds to central Florida.

Columbia and its crew of five astronauts are due to spend 16 days in orbit conducting scientific research with a pair of free-flying satelites. Two spacewalks are also planned to practice construction of the international space station.
